bids.title: Eagan Gymnasium Flooring Resurface
bids.description:
General work description:
 The City of Florissant, Missouri, is soliciting sealed bids from qualified flooring contractors to sand, refinish, and repaint the existing wood gymnasium floor at the James J. Eagan Civic Center.
 The project shall include the preparation and refinishing of the existing gymnasium floor, necessary minor repairs, installation of new gymnasium base and door thresholds, and the layout and painting of basketball, volleyball, and pickleball game lines on all three courts.
 All work shall be completed by qualified personnel experienced in commercial gymnasium flooring systems and athletic court finishes.
 Site Location:
 James J. Eagan Civic Center
1 James J. Eagan Drive
Florissant, MO 63033
 Site Visits:
 Contact: Jimmy Kirincich
Director of Parks and Recreation 
Phone: 314-461-2721
Email: [public contact omitted] 
 SCOPE OF WORK: 
 The successful contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, transportation, and incidentals necessary to complete the following work.
 A. Floor Preparation and Sanding
 Inspect the existing gymnasium floor and identify visible damage, worn finish, water-damaged areas, loose boards, and other conditions that may affect the project.

 Mechanically sand the existing wood gymnasium floor to remove the existing finish and prepare the surface for refinishing.

 Complete the sanding process in a manner that produces a uniform surface suitable for application of a new gymnasium floor finish.

 Perform minor surface preparation necessary to achieve a professional finished product.

 Remove sanding dust and debris generated by the contractor's work before applying finish materials.

 Notify the City of any significant concealed damage, deterioration, or repairs beyond the anticipated scope before proceeding with additional work.

 B. Floor Repairs
 Include replacement or repair of one damaged individual floorboard.

 Include repair of one approximately 1-foot-by-4-foot water-damaged floor area.

 Use replacement materials compatible with the existing wood flooring system, thickness, species, and appearance to the extent reasonably available.

 Ensure repaired areas are securely installed, properly sanded, and finished to blend with the surrounding floor.

 Identify any additional repairs required beyond the included work and provide separate pricing for such repairs before authorization by the City.

 C. Floor Finishing and Protective Coating
 Apply a complete gymnasium floor finishing system appropriate for an athletic wood floor.

 Provide a durable, uniform finish designed for indoor athletic use, including basketball, volleyball, and pickleball.

 Use commercial-grade materials specifically intended for gymnasium floors and compatible with the existing wood flooring.

 Apply all sealers, stains, finish coats, and other materials in accordance with the manufacturer's written instructions.

 Coordinate the application of game lines with the finishing process to ensure proper adhesion, appearance, and durability.

 Allow sufficient curing time before reopening the gymnasium for use.

 Provide the City with product data sheets, maintenance instructions, and recommended cure times for all finish materials.

 Color of stain should be approved by the city prior to purchasing. 
 The contractor shall identify the proposed finish manufacturer, product name, application system, and number of coats in the bid submission.
 D. Athletic Game Lines — All Three Courts
 The contractor shall lay out and paint new game lines for on each of the three gymnasium courts, for a total of eight court layouts.
 Basketball: One complete basketball game-line layout on each of the three courts.

 Volleyball: One complete volleyball game-line layout on two of the courts.

 Pickleball: One complete pickleball game-line layout on each of the three courts.

 All game lines shall be measured, laid out, and painted in accordance with the applicable sport dimensions and the City's approved layout.
 Sport Color Finish 
 Basketball Black Standard, High Contract 
 Volleyball Royal Blue Medium-Dark Blue 
 Pickleball Green Medium-to-Dark Green 

 The contractor shall:
 Verify existing court dimensions and field conditions before beginning work.

 Confirm all court layouts and line colors with the City before applying paint.

 Use commercial-grade, gymnasium-compatible line paint that is compatible with the specified floor finish.

 Apply clean, straight, clearly defined lines with consistent widths and no excessive bleeding, overspray, or irregular edges.

 Ensure that all lines are properly incorporated into the floor finishing system.

 Provide a proposed line-color schedule and court-layout drawing for City approval before painting.

 Ensure that the completed layouts provide clear differentiation between basketball, volleyball, and pickleball markings.

 No game lines shall be painted until the City has approved the proposed layout and colors in writing.
 E. Gymnasium Base and Door Thresholds
 Remove and replace existing gymnasium base as necessary to accommodate the refinishing project.

 Furnish and install new vented gymnasium base compatible with the existing floor system and facility conditions.

 Furnish and install new aluminum thresholds at all gymnasium doorways included in the project.

 Ensure the base and thresholds are securely installed, properly aligned, and free of sharp edges or trip hazards.

 Coordinate installation with the floor sanding and finishing process to prevent damage to newly finished surfaces.

 F. Final Cleaning and Project Closeout
 Remove contractor-generated debris, unused materials, and equipment from the work area.

 Leave the gymnasium floor and immediate work area clean and ready for City inspection.

 Provide written confirmation of the date the floor may safely be walked on and the date it may be returned to full athletic use.

 Provide all finish product information, warranties, care instructions, and maintenance recommendations.

 Complete a final walkthrough with the City's designated representative and correct deficiencies identified during the inspection.

 MATERIALS AND WORKMANSHIP 
 All materials shall be new, commercial-grade products specifically designed for use on indoor athletic wood flooring.
 All work shall be performed in accordance with the flooring and finish manufacturers' written requirements and applicable industry standards.
 The contractor shall be responsible for protecting existing walls, doors, equipment, bleachers, and other facility components from damage caused by the work. Any damage caused by the contractor shall be repaired at the contractor's expense.
 Substitutions of specified or proposed materials shall require prior written approval from the City.
 SITE INSPECTION AND EXISTING CONDITIONS 
 Bidders shall inspect the gymnasium before submitting a bid to evaluate the existing flooring, court layouts, access, doorways, base, and general project conditions.
 Bidders shall verify all measurements and quantities necessary to prepare an accurate proposal. Any dimensions or quantities provided by the City are for bidding purposes and shall be field-verified by the contractor.
 Questions regarding existing conditions or the scope of work shall be submitted to the City through Opengov bid questions before the bid deadline.
 PROJECT SCHEDULE AND FACILITY COORDINATION 
 The contractor shall provide a proposed project schedule identifying the anticipated start date, duration of work, finishing and curing periods, and expected completion date.
 All work shall be coordinated with the City's Parks and Recreation Department.
 The contractor shall not begin work until authorized by the City and shall not reopen the gymnasium for athletic use until the finish manufacturer’s required curing period has been satisfied and the City has approved the completed work.
 Any proposed work outside the City's approved schedule must receive prior written authorization.
 Timeline: 
 The contractor shall complete all work within the following project period:
 Start Date: February 8, 2027
 Final Cleanup and Inspection: Completed by March 19, 2027
 Time frames are subject to change due to this being a phased project with ceiling removal and painting prior to flooring resurface.
 Contractor should include their own estimated project timeline with bid 
 BID SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS 
 Bidders shall provide the following information:
 Total lump-sum price for completion of the base bid scope- See electronic pricing table.

 Manufacturer and product information for all proposed finish and line-paint materials.

 Proposed project schedule and estimated duration.

 List of exclusions, assumptions, and anticipated additional costs, if any.

 Description of warranty coverage for labor, materials, finish, and painted game lines.

 Relevant experience completing comparable gymnasium flooring projects.

 References for similar completed projects.

 Confirmation that the bidder has inspected the site or understands the site-inspection requirements.

 Performance bond is required within two week of fully executed contract. 
 Any work necessary to complete the stated scope shall be included in the base bid unless specifically identified as an exclusion and accepted by the City in writing.
 PRICING AND ALTERNATES 
 Bidders shall provide a firm lump-sum base bid for all work described in this document.
 Any additional repairs, major floor preparation, or work outside the base scope shall be listed separately with unit prices or a not-to-exceed amount, as applicable. Additional work shall not proceed without written authorization from the City.
 The City reserves the right to accept or reject proposed alternates and to award the project in accordance with applicable City procurement requirements.
 WARRANTY 
 The contractor shall provide written warranty information covering workmanship, finish application, and game-line adhesion and durability.
 The bid shall identify the duration of each warranty, the conditions covered, exclusions, and the process for requesting warranty service.
 FINAL ACCEPTANCE 
 The project shall be considered complete upon satisfactory completion of all specified work, removal of contractor-generated debris, submission of required closeout documentation, and written acceptance by the City of Florissant.
 The City reserves the right to identify and require correction of incomplete work, defects, or deficiencies that do not conform to the approved scope and specifications.
 GENERAL CONDITIONS 
 The contractor shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, codes, and regulations.

 The contractor shall maintain a safe and orderly work area throughout the project.

 The contractor shall be responsible for its employees, subcontractors, equipment, and materials.

 No additional work or charges shall be incurred without prior written approval from the City.

 The City reserves the right to reject any or all bids and to waive informalities in accordance with applicable procurement requirements.

 Alternates-Logo Installation: 
See attachments for logo
 The Contractor shall provide separate lump-sum pricing for the following:
 Alternate 1: Installation of an approximately 8-foot diameter City of Florissant center-court logo.

 Alternate 2: Installation of an approximately 10-foot diameter City of Florissant center-court logo.

 Pricing shall include all labor, materials, equipment, layout, painting, surface preparation, and protective finish associated with the completed logo installation.

bids.title: Eagan Civic Center Gymnasium Painting
bids.description:
General work description:
 The City of Florissant is seeking a qualified painting contractor to provide all labor, materials, equipment, tools, and supervision necessary to repaint the gymnasium at the James J. Eagan Civic Center. The project includes painting the gymnasium ceiling black and repainting the walls with a designated base color and three additional accent color stripes.
 All work shall be completed in a professional and workmanlike manner, with appropriate preparation and protection of the gymnasium floor, equipment, fixtures, and other existing surfaces.
 Scope of Work 
 A. Site Preparation and Protection
 Inspect all surfaces to be painted and notify the City of any existing damage or conditions that may affect the finished product.
 Protect the gymnasium floor, basketball goals, bleachers, doors, windows, lights, vents, electrical fixtures, and other surfaces or equipment not designated for painting.
 Provide all necessary lifts, scaffolding, ladders, and other equipment required to safely access the ceiling and upper wall areas.
 Properly prepare all surfaces before painting, including cleaning, removing loose or peeling paint, and addressing minor surface imperfections.
 Mask and cover all adjacent surfaces to prevent paint overspray, splatter, or other damage.
 B. Gymnasium Ceiling
 Paint the entire designated gymnasium ceiling black.
 Prepare the ceiling surface to promote proper paint adhesion and a consistent finish.
 Apply a suitable primer where necessary based on the existing surface and condition.
 Apply the number of finish coats necessary to achieve uniform color, coverage, and appearance, following the paint manufacturer's recommendations.
 Protect or carefully work around existing lighting, ventilation systems, fire protection equipment, and other ceiling-mounted fixtures unless otherwise directed by the City.
 The City will be removing the drop ceiling prior to painting. 
 C. Gymnasium Walls
 Prepare all designated wall surfaces for painting.
 Apply base color to the designated wall areas throughout the gymnasium.
 Apply three additional accent color stripes in locations and widths approved by the City of Florissant. two stipes at 2ft high
 one stripe at 3ft high 

 Ensure the accent strips are straight, level, consistent in width, and cleanly defined, with sharp edges and no visible bleeding between colors.
 Apply sufficient coats to provide uniform coverage and a consistent finish across all designated surfaces.
 Wall colors will be chosen with the selected vendor
 D. Paint and Materials
 Provide all paint, primer, masking materials, drop cloths, and related supplies necessary to complete the project.
 Use commercial-grade paints appropriate for an indoor municipal gymnasium, including ceiling and wall surfaces.
 Provide durable, washable wall paint suitable for a high-traffic recreation facility.
 Submit proposed paint products, colors, finishes, and manufacturer specifications to the City for approval before purchasing materials or beginning work.
 The City will approve all final colors and the layout of the two accent stripes before application.
 Schedule and Coordination 
 The contractor shall complete all work within the following project period:
 Start Date: January 18, 2027
 Final Cleanup and Inspection: Completed by February 5, 2027
 Final Completion February 8, 2027
 The contractor shall coordinate with the City of Florissant Parks and Recreation Department before beginning work. The contractor must confirm access requirements, staging locations, work hours, and any facility restrictions with the City.
 The contractor shall provide a proposed work schedule identifying surface preparation, ceiling painting, wall painting, accent stripe application, drying time, cleanup, and final inspection.
 All work must be performed in a manner that allows the City to resume normal facility operations by the required completion date.
 Contractor Responsibilities 
 The contractor shall:
 Furnish all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, and transportation required for the project.
 Maintain a safe, orderly work area and comply with all applicable federal, state, and local safety requirements.
 Ensure employees are properly trained to operate lifts and other equipment used for the project.
 Providing 3/4 inch plywood for protection while driving lifts across the gymnasium flooring. 
 Provide appropriate ventilation and follow all manufacturer requirements for application, drying, and curing.
 Prevent unauthorized access to the work area while painting or other hazardous operations are underway.
 Remove all masking materials, debris, empty containers, and other project-related waste upon completion.
 Repair or pay for damage caused by the contractor to City property, equipment, or existing finishes.
 Notify the City promptly of unforeseen conditions, delays, or additional work that may affect the schedule or project cost.
 Obtain written approval from the City before performing work outside the approved scope.
 Provide dumpster for all waste materials or remove debris from work area each day. 
 Quality Standards and Acceptance 
 All completed work shall be uniform in appearance and free of visible runs, drips, excessive brush marks, roller marks, overspray, missed areas, and unacceptable color variations.
 The three accent stripes shall have consistent widths and clean, straight edges. All painted surfaces shall receive adequate coverage in accordance with the paint manufacturer's specifications.
 The City reserves the right to inspect the work during the project and upon completion. Any deficiencies identified by the City shall be corrected by the contractor at no additional cost before final acceptance.
 Final acceptance will be contingent upon completion of the scope of work, satisfactory cleanup, correction of identified deficiencies, and approval by the City of Florissant.

 Estimated Square Footage: 
 Gymnasium Walls: 9,328 sq. ft.
 Ceiling Painting: 11, 187 sq. ft.
 All square footage measurements provided are estimates for bidding purposes only. The contractor shall independently verify all dimensions and actual paintable square footage prior to submitting a bid to ensure accurate pricing.

 Location: 
 James J. Eagan Civic Center
1 James J. Eagan Drive
Florissant, MO 63033

 Site Visits: 
 Contact: Jimmy Kirincich
Director of Parks and Recreation 
Phone: 314-461-2721
Email: [public contact omitted] 

 Alternates: 
 Logo Specifications-See attachment for logo
 Logo size: 12 feet wide × 12 feet tall.

 Application: Painted directly onto the wall.

 Colors: Match the official Parks & Recreation logo colors, including green, teal and brown. Colors palette to be provided to awarded contractor.

 Finish: Matte or low-sheen finish.

 Layout: Maintain the logo's original proportions.

 Surface preparation: Include layout, masking, surface preparation and painting in the bid.

bids.title: NIH MULTIPLE-AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT (MACC) FOR GENERAL CONSTRUCTION SERVICES
bids.agency: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
bids.description: SOLICITATION NOTICE MULTIPLE-AWARD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT (MACC) FOR GENERAL CONSTRUCTION SERVICES Solicitation No. 75N99027R00002 The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Acquisition and Logistics Management (OALM), Construction, A&E, Facilities and Leasing Office (CAFLO), anticipates issuing a Request for Proposals (RFP) for a Multiple-Award Construction Contract (MACC) to support the ongoing construction, alteration, repair, and maintenance requirements of the NIH Office of Research Facilities (ORF). The resulting contracts will be multiple-award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) construction contracts. Work will be authorized through individually issued task orders. This acquisition is anticipated to be conducted using competitive negotiated procedures under FAR Part 15. The Government intends to award multiple IDIQ construction contracts under FAR Subpart 16.5. Individual task orders will generally be awarded on a firm-fixed-price basis. The anticipated aggregate ceiling is $3 billion over an eight-year ordering period. Individual construction requirements will be competed through task orders among eligible MACC awardees in accordance with the ordering procedures established in the resulting contracts. The solicitation and resulting contracts will include procedures for adding and removing awardees during that period (on/off ramp). The initial seed-project scope estimated construction magnitude, applicable evaluation factors, and proposal submission requirements will be provided in the solicitation. SCOPE OF WORK Work under the MACC will primarily consist of general construction and may include, but is not limited to, maintenance, repair, painting, alterations, architectural work, mechanical systems, electrical systems, plumbing, heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC), civil work, earthwork, fencing, structural work, steel fabrication and welding, roofing, building renovations, demolition, new building construction, sustainable construction, design-bid-build, and design-build projects. Individual task orders may include one or more construction disciplines and will vary in size, scope, and complexity. All work will be performed in accordance with the requirements, specifications, drawings, and other documents applicable to each individual task order. LOCATIONS OF WORK The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Research Facilities (ORF) is the steward of NIH facilities and is responsible for the planning, design, construction, acquisition, maintenance and operation of NIH owned facilities, which include campuses in: · Bethesda, Maryland, · Frederick, Maryland, · Poolesville, Maryland, · Research Triangle Park, North Carolina, · The Rocky Mountain Laboratories (RML) in Hamilton, Montana. NAICS CODE AND SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. PSC Code: Y1JZ The corresponding small business size standard is $45 million. The NAICS code and small business size standard applicable to the initial seed project is also anticipated to be NAICS 236220 and $45 million, respectively. ACQUISITION STRATEGY AND ANTICIPATED AWARDS This acquisition will be conducted using full and open competition with reserves for eligible small business concerns. NIH anticipates awarding up to twenty (20) IDIQ contracts, consisting of: Approximately four (4) unrestricted/full-and-open awards; and Approximately sixteen (16) awards under small business reserves. The small business reserves are anticipated to include eligible concerns in the following categories: Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) Small Business; Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB); Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); and Participants in the SBA 8(a) Business Development Program. The solicitation will identify the anticipated distribution of the sixteen (16) reserve awards among the applicable small business and socioeconomic categories and will establish the eligibility requirements applicable to each reserve. NIH anticipates approximately four (4) awards in each socioeconomic reserve. Offerors must meet all applicable SBA eligibility requirements for the category under which they submit an offer. BONDING CAPACITY Offerors competing for an unrestricted/full-and-open award shall provide evidence from their surety demonstrating, at a minimum, bonding capacity of: $100 million for a single project; and $300 million aggregate bonding capacity. Offerors competing for an award under a small business reserve shall provide evidence from their surety demonstrating, at a minimum, bonding capacity of: $3 million for a single project; and $10 million aggregate bonding capacity. The solicitation will establish the specific documentation required to demonstrate bonding capacity. Performance and payment bond requirements applicable to individual construction task orders will be established in accordance with the solicitation, resulting contracts, applicable law and regulation, and the requirements of each task order. SMALL BUSINESS ELIGIBILITY AND JOINT VENTURES Offerors seeking an award under a small business reserve must satisfy all applicable SBA eligibility requirements for the applicable reserve category and NAICS code. The solicitation will identify any documentation required to establish an offeror's eligibility for the applicable small business or socioeconomic category. Small business concerns intending to submit an offer as a joint venture must comply with all applicable SBA joint venture requirements, including applicable requirements governing SBA-approved Mentor-Protégé relationships. Prospective offerors should consult current SBA regulations and guidance concerning joint ventures and the SBA Mentor-Protégé Program at www.sba.gov. CONTRACT CEILING AND ORDERING PERIOD The aggregate maximum value of all contracts and task orders awarded under the MACC will not exceed $3,000,000,000.00 over the entire ordering period. The $3 billion ceiling applies collectively to all MACC contracts and is not a per-contractor ceiling. The anticipated ordering period will consist of one eight-year ordering period. There is no anticipated annual or individual-contractor ceiling other than limitations established by the terms of the resulting contracts and individual task orders. MACC holders will remain eligible to compete for task orders, subject to the terms and conditions of their contracts, until expiration of the ordering period or exhaustion of the aggregate MACC ceiling, whichever occurs first. TASK ORDERS All work under the MACC will be authorized through individual task orders. Individual task orders will generally be awarded on a firm-fixed-price basis and will be separately priced. Each task order will establish the applicable scope of work, specifications and drawings, period of performance, applicable wage determination, bonding requirements, and other project-specific requirements. Task orders may be competed among all eligible MACC holders or restricted to eligible small business MACC holders in accordance with the ordering procedures established in the solicitation and resulting contracts. The anticipated maximum value of an individual task order is $800 million. Eligibility to compete for individual task orders may be subject to project-specific requirements, including required bonding capacity. GUARANTEED MINIMUM The Government's guaranteed minimum under each resulting IDIQ contract will be $1,000. The guaranteed minimum will be satisfied through issuance of a task order. The $1,000 guaranteed minimum is a contractual minimum obligation and should not be interpreted as establishing the minimum dollar value of all future task orders. SEED PROJECT The Government anticipates using an initial seed project in connection with the MACC source selection. The seed project, evaluation requirements, applicable specifications and drawings, and any other project-specific information will be identified in the solicitation. Successful MACC awardees that do not receive a seed-project task order will receive a task order sufficient to satisfy the applicable guaranteed minimum. SITE VISITS The Government anticipates conducting two organized site-visit sessions for the seed project on November 9, 2026. The solicitation will provide the session times, location, registration procedures, and other attendance instructions. To accommodate prospective offerors, the Government anticipates scheduling two site-visit sessions at the applicable location, one in the morning and one in the afternoon. Prospective offerors may attend only one scheduled session. bids.title: Z2DA--666-27-102 Lightning Protection Update B71N
bids.description: GENERAL: Introduction: An inspection for current code compliance of the lightning Protection System on Building 71N has been conducted and found the system needs upgrades and repairs to meet current NFPA 780 and UL96A standards. The Sheridan VA Medical Center needs the services of a qualified contractor to perform the needed lightning protection upgrades to the main hospital building 71N. Located on the Sheridan Wyoming Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC) campus, at 1898 Fort Road, Sheridan, Wyoming 82801. Statement of Work: Specifics a. Existing Conditions The existing lightning protection system (LPS) for Building 71N was installed in 1989 during the building s original construction. Overall, the system remains in fair condition, though it requires repair because several air terminals have become detached from their adhesive bonds to the roof surface. Air terminals are present at all high points of the structure, and all roof-mounted equipment and appurtenances are properly grounded. A main grounding bus connects the communication systems and possibly the electrical distribution system to the primary service ground. The specific location where the grounding system bonds together the structural steel, electrical system, lightning protection components, and plumbing to create an equipotential ground could not be identified during the assessment. A continuous grounding loop encircles Buildings 9, 71, and 71N, with all roof air terminals and down conductors tied into this loop. Down conductors descend to the loop at the corners of each of these buildings. Each air terminal has at least two separate grounding paths, satisfying current code requirements. No Transient Voltage Surge Suppression (TVSS) devices were observed in the system. The lower 8 feet of the ground down conductors are encased in PVC electrical conduit for protection. New Construction Recent construction has added large equipment and a screen wall to the roof, which now obstructs and interferes with the original positioning of the existing air terminals. This new equipment sits higher than the existing lightning protection system components, rendering the current air terminals ineffective at intercepting and safely directing lightning strikes to ground. Project Requirements To bring the existing lightning protection system (LPS) into compliance the following corrections are needed: Install Transient Voltage Surge Suppression (TVSS) devices at the building s main service panel. Establish proper bonding by interconnecting all electrical systems, communication systems, piping, and structural steel at the service entrance to create an equipotential ground. Repair all roof air terminals that have detached or pulled away from their adhesive mounts on the roof surface. Install new air terminals at both ends of each screen wall, with additional terminals spaced at 20-foot intervals along the top of each wall, and at the highest point of the HVAC ductwork. Install an air terminal at each corner of the new HVAC equipment. Connect all newly installed air terminals to the existing LPS using #2 bare copper conductors. After these corrections have been completed, a qualified inspection is required to verify full compliance with NFPA 780 and UL 96A standards. Upon successful inspection, a Master Label Certificate should be issued for the lightning protection system. General: Construction project is to be completed within 120 calendar days from date of Notice to Proceed (NTP). Contractor shall provide all equipment, materials, supplies, tools, software, supervision, and labor required for this project, which may include, but is not limited to, demolition work, providing negative pressure environment for work, and providing all new equipment, utilities, and room finishes as indicated in the plans and this SOW per VA construction standards. Safety submittals shall be completed and approved prior to the commencement of on-site construction work. Material selection submittals shall be completed and approved prior to ordering of materials for the project. The building tenants not in the construction areas will remain at work in the buildings during this construction. Patients will remain on the floor in areas not under construction, so the contractor shall make patient safety, and infection control measures a priority. The contractor shall coordinate work locations and schedules with VA COR to minimize impact to building tenants. All electrical, carpentry, architectural, mechanical work, product design, project management, and other work needed on this project shall be provided by the Contractor. All required electrical work, low, medium, or high voltage, shall be installed and terminated by the Contractor. No wiring or cabling shall be abandoned in place. All piping, cabling, and wiring shall be labeled. All cabling and patch cabling shall match the VAMC s station-standard colors. The installation must, at a minimum, be in accordance with all applicable codes indicated in the Department of Veterans Affairs Design Manuals and VA .PUBLICATIONS (Master Construction Specifications, Construction Standards, National Fire Protection Association (NFPA), Underwriters Laboratory (UL), International Building Code IBC 2003, and National Electric Code (NEC) building codes and standards and the VA Information Security Handbook 6500.6, 6550.0 etc.). The Contractor shall read and be familiar with the most current editions of the applicable codes, standards, guides, and manuals. Sources can be accessed at the Office of Construction and Facilities Management s Technical Information Library (TIL) (http://www.cfm.va.gov/TIL). Any penetrations through any floors, ceilings, or walls shall be fire caulked, or otherwise fire sealed, and shall be done in this contract to meet VA standards and NFPA standards. Contractor shall utilize the VAMC s station-standard fire stop products or approved equal product(s). The station-standard products are SpecSeal fire caulk product is SpecSeal SSS Intumescent Firestop Sealant; and, if needed, the SpecSeal Composite Sheet may be used in areas approved by the COR. The Contractor shall inquire of the COR if any existing equipment, fixtures, hardware, doors, frames, or any other property removed is desired to be retained by the VA for reuse elsewhere within the medical center, at the time of removal. If the VA desires to retain an item, the Contractor shall deliver it to a location designated by the COR. If the VA does not desire to retain an item, the Contractor shall dispose of it properly off-station. The new components installed shall be tested and commissioned, re-certified, and/or tested before VA acceptance. All testing parameters shall be provided by the Contractor with source references to the COR and 3rd-party reviewer before testing begins. Copies of all test reports must be provided to the COR. HVAC systems that have changes made to them as part of this project, beyond diffuser replacement, shall be tested and balanced by the Contractor. Any IT data cables installed or modified as part of this effort shall be tested after installation. Test methods and plans shall be coordinated with the COR. Any Med Gas systems modified as part of this effort shall be re-certified back to the closest shut-off in the system. The Contractor shall arrange for any required re-certification as part of this contract and shall provide plans and results to the COR for approval. Fire alarm devices that are tied into the building fire alarm system, that are replaced or relocated as a result of this work, shall be tested before that phase of the project is complete. The Contractor shall arrange for all required fire alarm testing. If a building s fire alarm system is under warranty, testing must be accomplished by the contractor who holds the warranty. Any fire sprinklers that are relocated as part of this project shall be reviewed and approved by VA Safety prior to installation. All fire sprinkler work shall be coordinated with VA Safety so as to avoid accidentally setting off the system. At the conclusion of the project, the Contractor shall provide the VA and AE with a red-lined set of construction drawings, showing any as-built variations from the plans, as called for in the specifications. The Contractor must repair any damage caused by the Contractor or their subcontractors during this project. Repairs shall be done timely and will be coordinated with the COR. Repairs shall be of equal or better quality and finish than the existing that was damaged. Contractor s work hours shall be between 7:30am-4:00pm Monday-Friday, unless otherwise coordinated with, and approved in advance by, the COR. Noisy work shall not begin prior to 7:30am. Contractors shall not work on weekends, or federal holidays as specified by U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM), unless approved in advance by the COR or CO. For approved weekend or holiday work, Contractor must adjust their workers pay accordingly at no additional cost to the VA. The Contractor shall repair any disturbed earth around and in the construction areas. This shall include: Removing any rocks or clumps that have been brought to the surface. Filling in any ruts or depressions with approved fill material, such that the areas are level or at the required slope. Returning the surface cover to what is was before the project, or as called out in the project drawings. In the case of grass, the contractor shall provide topsoil as necessary to provide a good medium for grass growth. If the area(s) cannot be covered by the VA sprinkler system, then the Contractor shall provide for the watering of the new grass until it is established. Any area that the grass does not take to shall be reseeded under the warranty period. The Contractor shall replace any trees, shrubs, or other plants damaged or destroyed during construction, per the project landscape drawings, at no additional cost to VA. Safety and Security: The Contractor shall follow all safety specifications and shall always have an OSHA-30 certified person on-site, at each work location, overseeing the construction. All other Contractors and subcontractors working on-site shall have at least OSHA-10 certifications. Some work will be in medical areas of the hospital, on floors with patients present, so the contractor shall plan for infection control measures to include dust containment, negative pressure, and cleanup to hospital standards. The Contractor will, with the participation of the COR, complete an Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA), using the VA forms and process, and Contractor shall implement all protection measures called for in the risk assessment. For work on an active mental health unit, the Contractor shall follow strict tool control and access control in construction areas. Any patients found in construction areas shall be immediately reported to ward staff and the COR. The Contractor shall read and follow the current version of the FMS Safety Plan, which outlines expectations for tool control and safety on-station, [as well as stricter requirements for work on the Acute Psychiatric Ward (APU) located on the 2nd floor of Building 8 (e.g., Rule of Two minimum with one person overseeing the work at all times). Work on APU is not in-scope for this project.] General Contractor shall distribute the FMS Safety plan to their workers and subcontractors. General Contractor shall note this training in their daily logs. General station safety requirements: It is vitally important to keep tools and other items that offer a patient the opportunity for self-harm under control at all times. Tools, extension cords, and similar items should not be left out unattended where patients can gain access to them. This includes in the open backs of contractor vehicles, trailers, laydown areas, tool carts, etc.. No repairs are authorized under this contract. The purpose of this effort is to document the existing condition of the entire DWV system and provide recommendations for future corrective actions. bids.title: J061--ELECTRICAL TESTING (SOLICITATION)
bids.description: 3-Year Electrical Testing and Repair Contract Performance Work Statement (PWS) General Requirements: Contractor shall furnish all supplies, materials, equipment, personnel/labor and technical supervision required to perform inspections, repairs, testing, cleaning, calibrations and adjustments on the electrical power distribution system and associated equipment at the Hampton Veterans Affairs Medical Center within the allotted time frame of this contract. This is a 4160 volt primary system that includes various secondary voltages and both emergency and normal power sources. A comprehensive list of equipment is included in this contract as well as a dollar amount to be set aside for repairs. All inspections and testing procedures must meet the criteria of the original equipment manufacturer along with the latest editions of the following codes, standards and specifications listed: ANSI, IEEE, ICEA, NETA, NEMA, NFPA, JCAHO and VA regulations. The contractor shall be responsible for supplying all portable power required to power up any and all test equipment necessary throughout these tests. The use of normal or emergency building power will not be allowed. The contractor shall be responsible for securing all manufacturers information, curves, data, procedures and any other information necessary to conduct specific tests on equipment and systems. Prior to beginning field-testing, the testing organization shall submit test procedures and a detailed test schedule to the Electrical Supervisor for each item of equipment to be field-tested. No testing is to be performed until after the test procedures and schedules have been approved. The contractor shall be responsible for all coordination between Dominion Virginia Power (if applicable), station supervisory personnel and test personnel for scheduling shut-downs, system tests and tests on system components. The V.A Medical Center Electrical Staff will be responsible for conducting the actual scheduled outages and reenergizing of circuits and components on V.A. premises and V.A. owned equipment only. Lockout/Tagout of this equipment will be performed jointly between the V. A. Medical Center Electricians and the Contractor. The contractor will be responsible for removal and replacement of any and all breakers needing to be tested. All breakers being removed will be properly reinstalled. Any and all conductors removed from a breaker will be properly terminated back to that breaker and any and all lugs will be properly torqued to manufacturers specifications. Testing shall commence and be completed within nine (9) consecutive days, beginning on a Saturday and ending on the following Sunday. The specific dates shall be coordinated with the COTR. All outages shall be scheduled with the COTR two weeks in advance of testing start date. Testing dates may change due to inclement weather, however, the COTR shall first be notified and approve any changes necessary. Contractor shall anticipate all work to be done after normal working hours. Outages will be scheduled at night between the hours of 5:00 p.m. and midnight and between the hours of 7:00 am and 5:00 p.m. on weekends. However the Contractor should be prepared to work longer hours should problems develop to assure restoration of power. Daytime hours, during the week, may be approved under certain circumstances if there is no impact to building occupants. This would be a rare instance, thus Contractor should anticipate overtime hours for all contract requirements. Equipment Repairs: Minor repairs shall include but not be limited to such items as loose bolts, loose or broken lugs, wiring terminals, heaters, malfunctioning targets, dirty/high resistance connections, etc and shall be corrected on site during testing if possible. Repair or replacement of larger items such as breakers shall also be performed during this outage if possible. However if parts are not readily available, these items will be repaired or replaced under a separate smaller outage and will be scheduled after parts or components are available. Contractor shall set aside a line item not to exceed $50,000 for repair or replacement parts with this contract. All repairs shall be invoiced under this line item at the conclusion of the contract. This amount is to be used for bidding purposes. However a materials breakdown will be required with the final invoice and Contractor shall be paid actual costs with appropriate mark up s up to $50,000 for parts. Contractor is not to exceed this amount without prior written approval of the Contracting Officer. Minimum Equipment Test Requirements: 5 KV AIR CIRCUIT BREAKERS 1. The breakers will be removed from their compartments. The compartments shall be cleaned and inspected. Shutters shall be cleaned, inspected, and tested for proper operation. The racking mechanisms shall also be cleaned, lubricated and tested for proper operation. 2. All cable termination s, both primary and secondary, shall he checked for signs of overheating, proper tightness and support. 3. All exposed bus connections shall be checked for signs of overheating and for proper tightness. 4. The arc chutes will be removed, cleaned and inspected. 5. The entire breaker and the mechanism will be inspected. 6. The entire operating mechanism will be thoroughly cleaned, lubricated and exercised. 7. All of the interior components of the circuit breaker will be thoroughly cleaned. 8. The contacts and current carrying assemblies will be inspected for burning, pitting, arcing, worn fingers, garter springs etc. 9. The contacts will be cleaned and anti-oxidant grease will be applied to the breaker s main contacts. 10. The breaker contact resistance will be measured and recorded. 11. An insulation resistance test will be performed and results recorded. 12. The breaker will then be closed manually to ensure proper closing and trip operations. 13. Any and all interlocks will be checked and proper operation will be verified. 14. The breaker will be electrically operated when test stands are available, or the breaker will be operated from its cubicle, if the system allows. 15. All indicating devices such as lights, flags, switches etc. shall be tested for proper operation. Any that are not operating properly shall be repaired at that time if possible. 16. All heat strips throughout the enclosure shall be made operational, by repair or replacement, prior to completion of inspection. ENCLOSED AIR BREAK SWITCHES (MEDIUM VOLTAGE) 1. After shutdown, the entire switch mechanism will be cleaned and inspected. 2. The switch contacts will be checked for proper alignment. Anti-oxidant grease will be applied to the main contacts. 3. The switch s arcing contacts will be checked for the proper opening sequence relative to the main contacts. 4. The switch s operating mechanism will be inspected for wear and proper operation. The entire mechanism will be cleaned and lubricated. All interlocks will be tested and proper operation will be verified. 5. Fuses will be inspected; size and type will be recorded. 6. All phase isolation barriers will be cleaned, and the barriers will be checked for contamination and corona damage. 7. All insulators will be cleaned and visually inspected for cracks and chips. 8. All exposed bus and cable connections will be checked for proper tightness and for evidence of overheating, burning or tracking. 9. All lightning arrestors will be cleaned and inspected for broken or damaged porcelain and subjected to an insulation resistance test. Results shall be recorded. 10. All ground connections will be inspected and repaired if found to be inadequate. 11. Contact resistance and insulation resistance tests will be performed, where possible, and the results recorded. 12. All heat strips throughout the enclosure shall be made operational, by repair or replacement, prior to completion of inspection. OIL-FILLED TRANSFORMERS 1. The transformers will be inspected for leaks, poor seals and or gaskets, and for proper oil levels. 2. The transformer tank and its cooling fins will be inspected for rust, chipped paint, dents, and proper connection to ground. 3. All of the bushings will be cleaned, inspected for cracks and or chips. proper tightness. and evidence of overheating. 4. All gauges and alarm devices will he inspected, recorded and reset where applicable. 5. Insulation resistance tests of each transformer winding will he performed, where possible and the results recorded. 6. Turns ratio test shall be performed and recordings documented. 7. The oil will be sampled and tested in accordance with ASTM procedures. All sampling devices used will be new, clean and sealed with thread sealant. Drip pans shall be installed under all the valves prior to any oil removal. The contractor will clean up any and all oil lost during sampling. DRY-TYPE TRANSFORMERS 1. Check enclosure for dents, loose bolts, proper ventilation, anchoring and grounding. 2. The inside of the transformer shall be cleaned and all electrical terminations will be checked for signs of overheating and proper tightness. 3. Insulation resistance tests of each transformer winding will be performed, where possible and the results recorded. 4. Turns ratio test shall be performed and recordings documented. SWITCHGEAR AND STRUCTURE 1. After power shutdown, the entire switchgear interior will be thoroughly cleaned. 2. Exposed bus connections will be checked for proper tightness. 3. All of the bus insulators will be thoroughly cleaned and visually inspected for cracks and chips. 4. All control switches, auxiliary relays, and devices will be cleaned, lubricated (if applicable), and checked for proper operation. 5. All disconnect switches will be cleaned, lubricated, adjusted and an anti-oxidant grease applied to the contacts. 6. The lightning arrestors will be cleaned and subjected to an insulation resistance test. Results will be recorded. 7. An insulating resistance test of the bus will be performed. Results will be recorded. LOW VOLTAGE AIR CIRCUIT BREAKERS 1. Each breaker will have its inspection covers removed and the breaker will be thoroughly cleaned. 2. All contact surfaces will be cleaned to assure maximum conductance. 3. Anti-oxidant grease will be applied to the breaker s main contacts. 4. Mechanisms will be checked and lubricated. The mechanical operation will be verified. 5. A current equal to 90 and 110 percent of the breaker s trip coil setting will be applied to verify proper pick-up of the tripping mechanism. 6. Primary injection testing shall be performed in order to verify that all long-time, short time, instantaneous and ground fault set points are properly set. Those that are not shall be properly adjusted and retested. Units will be tested by passing multiples of their ratings through each phase of the breaker. The resultant trip-times will be recorded. 7. Contact resistance will be measured and contacts will be adjusted, where possible, for maximum surface contact and pressure. Value of contact resistance tests will be recorded. 8. An insulation resistance test will be performed from each pole to the other two poles and to ground, and the values recorded. 9. On draw out breakers, the breaker carriage and racking mechanism will be cleaned and lubricated. OIL DISCONNECT SWITCHES 1. The switch mechanism will be opened where applicable. 2. The switch contacts will he inspected and cleaned where applicable. 3. The switch s operating mechanism will he visually and manually inspected for wear, operation, binding and then cleaned and lubricated. 4. The switch s insulating fluid will be sampled. tested and fluid levels returned to normal. 5. The complete unit will then be reassembled and tested for proper operation. 6. The contractor will clean up any and all oil lost during sampling. 7. Insulation resistance tests will be performed where accessible and results recorded. MOLDED CASE CIRCUIT BREAKERS (ELECTRICAL TEST) 1. Each molded case circuit breaker will be inspected

The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) Fort Drum, NY is seeking to identify multiple Small Businesses with the interest and resources to enter into a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for General Construction Services under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 236220 Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The small business size standard for this industry is $45 million in average annual revenue. The Product Service Code is Z2QA Repair or Alteration of Real Property (Public or Private). MICC-Fort Drum anticipates procuring construction projects valued between the Micro-purchase Threshold and the Simplified Acquisition Threshold on a competitive basis through the BPA for General Construction Services. Construction projects under the BPA would include but not be limited to the following: Provide all necessary resources, management, personnel, materials, supervision, transportation, supplies, and all equipment, except Government Furnished Property (GFP) to facilitate all phases of work in connection with various general construction projects on Fort Drum, NY. This would include new work, additions, alterations and maintenance and repair of real property facilities and structures. Insurance is required for these types of projects; and information on required insurance amounts will be included in the Statement of Work. Contractors with a BPA must be capable of obtaining the payment bonds required for construction projects valued between $35,000.00 and the Simplified Acquisition Threshold. Contractors unable to meet this bonding requirement will not be considered for issuance of a BPA. Where site visits are offered and attended, the prime BPA Contractor must represent themselves (subcontractors cannot represent a prime contractor on site visits or in response to any request for information or quote). BPA contractors shall comply with FAR 52.222-6 Construction Wage Rate Requirements (formerly Davis-Bacon Act). Each project will be competitively procured, and the Government will incorporate the most current Davis Bacon wage determination in effect at time of award. Davis Bacon wage determinations are located at https://sam.gov/content/wage-determinations. In accordance with FAR Part 36.101-4 Advance Notices and Solicitations, contractors are required to submit requests for equitable adjustment as a result of change orders to the issuing Contracting Officer. Contractors are required to acknowledge the change order within 30 days and are to submit their request for adjustment which includes all supporting documents as soon as possible, but not later than the required completion date of the contract. In the attached full synopsis, a table is included which displays the agency’s past performance, for the period of three fiscal years, regarding the time required to definitize equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts. When establishing these BPAs, the Government will consider price and socio-economic status. BPAs will be evaluated annually and may remain in place for up to five (5) years. Annual review of BPAs will be performed to determine whether the Government is receiving fair and reasonable pricing, usage, and participation, which may result in either continuing the BPA or early discontinuation. Early discontinuation may result if the Government no longer has a requirement for the general construction services provided by the Contractor. MICC-Fort Drum anticipates a maximum of 10 contractors holding a BPA for general construction services. A list of interested vendors will be maintained. The Contractor must be registered in Wide Area Work Flow (WAWF) for contract payment. To register and access WAWF, go to https://piee.eb.mil/. As prescribed in DFARS 252.204-7007, interested parties must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) under NAICS Code 236220. Representations and Certifications must also be on record. SAM registration is free and done through the website at https://www.sam.gov. Per the authority of FAR Clause 52.219.3(c) Notice of HUBZone Set-Aside or Sole-Source Award, this procurement will be 100% set aside for Historically Underutilized Business (HUB) Zone small businesses. bids.title: Construction of Chilled Water Plant and Site Utility Upgrades at VA Medical Center in West Haven, CT
bids.description: The scope of the chilled water plant replacement consists of the demolition of the existing chilled water plant (building 16a) and construction of a new multi-story chilled water plant to include chillers, cooling towers, pumps, and all associated mechanical and electrical equipment. Due to the close proximity of the existing fuel tank farm adjacent to the existing chilled water plant, a new fuel tank farm will need to be constructed as part of the project, which primarily serves the central boiler plant, requiring close coordination with the medical center and ongoing related projects.The scope of the site utility upgrades consists of the replacement and upgrade of the existing fire protection water main and the domestic water main from Campbell Avenue to Building 15. Site utility upgrades also include providing utility main loops of chilled water supply and return, steam supply, condensate return, domestic water supply, and fire protection water supply which will originate from the new chilled water plant and back-feed to Building 1. The work also includes the installation of redundant electrical feeder from the utility demarcation point to Building 19 and coordination with the local electrical utility provider to provide further electrical redundancy offsite as well. In addition, new water storage tanks will be constructed. This project involves civil/site, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural, geotechnical, and architectural disciplines. The project must also comply with the DVAs Physical Security Resiliency Design Requirements (PSRDM). It is expected that the chilled water plant will be constructed to meet USGBC LEED Silver certification. The work is located adjacent to and within an active Medical Center campus which will be operational at all times. Impact to on-going operations must be kept to a minimum and carefully coordinated with the Contracting Officer and VAMC staff. In addition, the work area is constrained due to the active medical center operations which will limit laydown and storage areas during construction.

bids.description: Amendment 0003 is hereby posted. ________________________________________________________________________ Amendment 0002 is hereby posted. ________________________________________________________________________ Amendment 0001 is hereby posted. ________________________________________________________________________ The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS), is seeking a qualified contractor for construction services for the Gate 7 Parking Garage at the St. Elizabeths West Campus in Southeast Washington, DC. GSA anticipates awarding a single Firm-Fixed-Price construction contract for the new construction of the Gate 7 Parking Garage and associated site, utility, security, stormwater, landscape, and infrastructure improvements. The project will support the operational needs of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) at the St. Elizabeths West Campus. This acquisition is for construction services only. The project design is being completed separately by GSA’s Architect of Record, ZGF. The construction solicitation is based on Issued for Construction drawings, specifications, and related contract documents. The work to be performed under the terms of this contract includes, but is not limited to, furnishing all management, supervision, subcontractors, labor, materials, supplies, tools, equipment, coordination, quality control, testing, inspections, commissioning support, and closeout documentation necessary to construct the Gate 7 Parking Garage in accordance with the contract documents. The project includes construction of a new multi-level parking garage with associated surface parking, access and screening infrastructure, and related campus improvements. The anticipated scope includes, but is not limited to: Site development, clearing, grading, excavation, and civil infrastructure improvements Utility relocations, extensions, tie-ins, and connections Substructure construction, including foundations, slab-on-grade, excavation support, waterproofing, and retaining walls Parking garage structure, including structural framing, parking decks, ramps, stairs, elevators, roof assemblies, and related structural components Mechanically ventilated parking garage systems, including ventilation equipment, shafts, ductwork, louvers or openings, controls, electrical power, life-safety interfaces, testing, balancing, and commissioning support Exterior façade and building envelope construction, including a classical architectural brick façade with openings Exterior doors, windows, louvers, waterproofing, sealants, flashings, and related envelope components Mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, fire alarm, emergency communications, lighting, controls, IT, telecommunications, electronic security, access control, CCTV, parking guidance, and related systems Physical security elements, including vehicle barriers, bollards, gates, credentialing areas, and screening-related infrastructure Roadway, shuttle, pedestrian circulation, hardscape, landscape, site lighting, signage, and related site improvements Stormwater management facilities, erosion and sediment control, and environmental protection measures Testing, inspections, commissioning support, training, warranties, as-built documentation, BIM/COBie deliverables where applicable, and project closeout The Gate 7 Parking Garage will be constructed within the active St. Elizabeths West Campus, a high-security federal campus and National Historic Landmark. The contractor will be required to coordinate construction activities with ongoing campus operations, security requirements, occupied facilities, existing utilities, shuttle operations, adjacent work, traffic and access impacts, and protection of historic and environmental resources. The contractor may also be required to coordinate with District of Columbia agencies or authorities, as applicable, for traffic control, haul routes, public space, utility, roadway, permit, or other construction-related requirements. All work shall conform to applicable GSA requirements, the 2026 PBS Core Building Standards, contract drawings and specifications, campus security requirements, applicable codes and standards, and project-specific requirements. The estimated cost range for construction is between $120,000,000.00 and $160,000,000.00. The intended project delivery method is a Phased Acquisition procurement using a Two-Phase Construction Concept. Specific security requirements will be contained in the solicitation. FUNDS AVAILABILITY: Funds are not presently available for this contract. The Government’s obligation under this contract is contingent upon the availability of appropriated funds from which payment for contract purposes can be made. bids.title: Z2DA--FY27 EHRM | 657-21-702JC EHRM Training And Administrative Space Construction - St Louis John Cochran
bids.description: INTRODUCTION The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) anticipates soliciting bids and subsequently awarding a single firm-fixed-price contract for the design-bid-build EHRM Training and Administrative Space Construction project at the St. Louis VA Health Care System (VAHCS) John Cochran campus located at 915 North Grand BLVD, St. Louis, MO 63106. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The VA Saint Louis Health Care System John Cochran Division requires a construction contractor to perform upgrades in support of the Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) program. The construction area is located on the first floor of Building 2 and includes both training and administrative spaces. This project includes the execution of Phases 2, 3, and 4 of the associated design plans. Phase 2 addresses the North Training Rooms (Rooms 139, 140, 141, 142), totaling approximately 2,000 square feet. Work includes upgraded power and data infrastructure and new flooring and wall finishes. Phase 3 addresses the South Training Rooms (Rooms 126, 127, 128), totaling approximately 1,800 square feet. Work includes upgraded power and data infrastructure and new flooring and wall finishes. Additionally, Phase 3 includes the renovation of a 130-square-foot breakroom, with new floor and wall finishes, casework, a new sink, and a cold-water tie-in for an ice machine. Phase 4 addresses multiple areas: renovation of an approximately 1,400-square-foot corridor with new floor and wall finishes; upgrades to two offices (approximately 150 square feet each) with upgraded power and data infrastructure and new flooring and wall finishes; and upgrades to an existing data closet, including new floor and wall finishes, installation of an additional server rack with associated equipment, and replacement of the existing mini-split HVAC unit. Note: Phase 1 is excluded from this scope, as it was completed under a separate contract. Note: All power and data drops originally indicated as floor-mounted shall now be wall-mounted, as shown on revised drawings EP101 and TN101. Installation must match these updated sheet details; no floor-mounted outlets are permitted. ADMINISTRATIVE The solicitation will be issued as an Invitation for Bids (IFB) conducted in accordance with FAR part 14 and will be evaluated in accordance with the procedures listed in the solicitation. The solicitation will be issued as a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Offers received from other than SDVOSB concerns will not be considered. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 with a size standard of $45.0 million. The solicitation will be issued in early to mid-October 2026. The period of performance is approximately 150 calendar days from the issuance of the notice to proceed. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $250,000 and $500,000. This notice is not a request for competitive offers. All questions must be submitted in writing to the issuing office via email to [public contact omitted]. Telephone calls will not be accepted.

bids.title: 91st Cyber Operations Center – Progressive Design-Build Other Transaction Agreement
bids.description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, on behalf of the Department of the Air Force (DAF), is issuing this Program Solicitation to identify a Design-Build Team for the 91st Cyber Operations Center at Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA), Lackland Air Force Base, Texas. The project involves the design and construction of an approximately 42,000-square-foot, multi-story facility to support the mission requirements of the Air Combat Command 91st Cyber Operations Squadron. The facility will be designed and constructed to meet applicable security and technical standards for a mission-critical cyber operations environment. This acquisition will use a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) delivery model executed under an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement pursuant to 10 U.S.C. § 2808a. The acquisition will be conducted in two phases: Phase 1—Design and Pre-Construction Services: The selected Design-Build Team will collaborate with the Government to refine project requirements, advance the design, validate cost and schedule, and support development of the Phase 2 scope. Phase 2—Construction Packages: Subject to successful Phase 1 performance, successful negotiation, required approvals, authorization, and availability of funds, the Government may authorize subsequent construction packages through Agreement Amendment. Anticipated packages include: Phase 2A—Site/Civil and Early Construction: Site development, civil work, and other early construction activities. Phase 2B—Building Construction: Final design completion and construction of the 91st Cyber Operations Center facility. The Government may authorize additional construction packages, as appropriate. The Government is under no obligation to proceed with Phase 2A, Phase 2B, or any additional package. The Government will use a two-step, qualifications-based selection process: White Paper Submission and Evaluation Pitch Meetings, by invitation only Interested Design-Build Teams are invited to submit a White Paper in accordance with the solicitation and its attachments. The White Paper is the only submission required at this time. White Papers must address all requirements in Attachment 1, Request for White Paper Submission Requirements. Questions: All questions must be submitted through the ProjNet Bidder Inquiry System no later than 11 November 2026, in accordance with the solicitation instructions. White Paper Due Date: White Papers are due no later than 17 November 2026 at 1400 Central Time. Submission Method: Submit White Papers by email to the Solicitation Points of Contact identified in the solicitation. Required Email Subject Line: “White Paper for 91st Cyber Operations Center” Refer to the attached Program Solicitation, Attachment 1—Request for White Paper Submission Requirements, and Attachment 2—Project Requirements Document for the complete project scope, submission instructions, evaluation approach, and applicable requirements.

This scope of work is to build an addition and renovate the Central Utility Building (CUB). The CUB supplies chilled water, hot water, low conductivity water, and makeup water to various lab buildings and systems. These systems serve both comfort cooling and heating needs, as well as process cooling and utility requirements. It is vital to Fermilab’s mission that CUB be revitalized and expanded, ensuring the ability to serve existing and future loads. The General contractor shall furnish all required supervision, labor, materials, tools, plant and appurtenances necessary to perform diligently and fully all work as described in the drawings and technical specifications. All work includes transportation, overhead, bonding costs, safety oversight, quality control oversight, and supervision as required to construct the project described in the drawings, technical specification and the detailed description contained herein. The critical schedule constraint for construction of this project is Fermilab’s accelerator shutdown, with an anticipated scheduled start on January 1, 2028, and anticipated end date of January 1, 2030- these dates may change depending on the needs of the Lab. The General Contractor must start their on-site efforts, and complete the construction scope under this contract, within the shutdown window. This project includes the following milestones: Milestone 1 – Issuance of Notice to Proceed (NTP) to 30th December 2027. This milestone is intended for completion of necessary submittals and RFIs, approval of shop drawings for fabrication and procurement. Milestone 2 – 3rd January 2028; This milestone marks the point where construction work may begin. Milestone 3 – 31st January 2029; AUP 1 CUB Extension complete. Milestone 4 – 29th June 2029; AUP 2 Existing CUB Upgrade complete. Milestone 5 – 28th September 2029; Completion of CUB- including all remedial work following removal of site trailers.

bids.description: VA Northern California Health Care System 612A4-27-018 Page 4 of 5 Statement of Work Replace B650 3rd and 2nd Flooring Project #612A4-27-018 General Intention: The purpose of this project is to replace flooring, resilient base, stainless steel corner guards, and paint throughout B650 3rd and 2nd Floor of the Sacramento Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC) of VA Northern California Healthcare System (VANCHCS). Contractor shall furnish all labor and materials needed to perform all demolition, replacement, and installation required by this scope as required by specifications. Visits to the site by bidders may be made only by appointment with the Contracting Officer (CO) for the project. A preliminary/pre-proposal site visit is strongly encouraged and shall be coordinated with the Contracting Officer Representative (COR). Location of work; the geographic location for service(s) are the following areas: Sacramento VA Medical Center 10535 Hospital Way Mather, CA 95655 Buildings: 650 3rd and 2nd Floors The contractor shall consider that there are no staging areas available within the facility premises. If necessary, staging areas may be put into effect at the discretion of the COR, depending on availability. The Contractor shall note that there is absolutely NO Contractor employee parking in Patient Parking designated areas. VANCHCS will not invalidate or make reimbursement for parking violations for the Contractor under any conditions. The contractor will be responsible for disposing of all equipment components and trash demolished or replaced as part of this project. The contractor is responsible for following infection control procedures per VA specifications and site infection control protocols. Work during normal hours may only be scheduled if it is planned at least three weeks in advance for a specific location and approved by the appropriate VA personnel. Any work activities that generate noise or disruption sufficient to impact patient care, disturb patients, or interfere with staff operations must be conducted only after normal working hours or on weekends. The contractor is responsible for coordinating with VA COR to ensure all work scheduling complies with this requirement and must provide notification of planned work at least three weeks prior to commencement. Emergency work or exceptions to this schedule must be requested in writing and approved by the CO. All work shall comply with all applicable federal, state, local and VA regulations and requirements. The Contractor shall refer to Specification Section 09 06 00, Schedules for Finishes, for the products and finishes required under this contract. The Contractor shall furnish the specified products or an equivalent product that meets or exceeds all requirements of the specified product, including, as applicable, quality, performance, durability, compatibility, dimensions, appearance, finish, color, and warranty requirements. The proposed product shall be similar in appearance and shall match the color, texture, pattern, and finish of the specified product to the satisfaction of VA Engineering. The Contractor shall submit product data, samples, color charts, and other information necessary for VA Engineering s evaluation and approval. The contractor shall remove and install new accessories associated with the flooring. Carpet and luxury vinyl tiles to include, but not limited to, subfloors, carpet tack strips, carpet padding, and vinyl glue. The contractor shall paint all rooms located on the 2nd and 3rd floors of Building 650 per specification Section 09 06 00, Schedule of Finishes. The Contractor shall furnish the specified products or an equivalent product that meets or exceeds all requirements of the specified product, including, as applicable, quality, performance, durability, compatibility, dimensions, appearance, finish, color, and warranty requirements. The proposed product shall be similar in appearance and shall match the color, texture, pattern, and finish of the specified product to the satisfaction of VA Engineering. The contractor shall anticipate repairing up to 20% of the drywall surface area in each room as needed to ensure a uniform and high-quality finish. The contractor is responsible for providing all necessary materials, labor, and equipment to complete both the repair and painting work. The VA will provide a paint plan as the installation date approaches. bids.description: The United States Coast Guard Deputy Commandant for Systems (DCS) is issuing this combined synopsis/solicitation on behalf of the Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC) to award a firm-fixed-price service contract, as detailed in the attached Statement of Work. This requirement consists of performing all on-site labor and services to remove the existing fire suppression system and install a new water mist system and fire alarm control panel in support of the USCGC SCIOTO. All work must be performed on-site at 221 Mississippi Drive, Keokuk, IA 52632. The planned Period of Performance (PoP) is from 15Nov26 through 23Nov26. This acquisition is a 100% total small business set-aside under NAICS code 238220, with a corresponding small business size standard of $19.0 million. The applicable Product Service Code is N042. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quote conforming to the solicitation is most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors will be used to evaluate offers: 1. Technical Capability (Pass/Fail) 2. Past Performance (Pass/Fail) 3. Total Price A quotation must receive an Acceptable rating for all non-price factors to be eligible for award. Among all acceptable quotations, award will be made to the responsible offeror submitting the lowest evaluated price. To establish Technical Capability (Pass/Fail), the quotation must demonstrate a clear understanding of the work statement requirements, conform strictly to all specifications in the attached Statement of Work, and provide any adequate capability and corporate experience documentation required by the solicitation. Failure to meet these criteria will render the quotation unacceptable. The Government will evaluate recent (completed within the last three years) and relevant past performance to assess the likelihood of successful performance. Past performance will be evaluated on an acceptable or unacceptable basis. To receive an acceptable rating, past performance must demonstrate a rating of satisfactory or higher performance of similar work. Offerors without recent or relevant past performance will be assessed as "Neutral" and considered acceptable for award. Past performance demonstrating marginal or below performance is unacceptable. Offerors shall identify all subcontractors anticipated to perform work under this contract. For each subcontractor, the offeror shall provide the subcontractor’s name, address, point of contact, phone number, the specific work items/specifications they will perform, and the percentage of work they will execute. Submit offers electronically via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government does not prescribe a specific quotation format. Offerors must submit a quotation that clearly identifies the items offered and demonstrates compliance with the stated requirements. Submissions must be complete, clear, and presented in a format that allows effective evaluation by the Government. Submit all questions via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government will not accept telephone inquiries. Submit offers on a firm-fixed-price basis. Prices must be all-inclusive and must cover all costs associated with providing the services, including but not limited to manufacturing, packaging, handling, transportation, duties, tariffs, fees, and any other costs. The Government may consider offers nonresponsive if they include conditional pricing, price escalation language, or statements indicating that prices are subject to adjustment based on future costs or fees. The Government intends to evaluate offers and make award without discussions; therefore, offerors should submit their best offer with initial submission. The Statement of Work and the list of applicable FAR provisions and clauses are attached to this notice.
